q1: SELECT A.PROJECT_ID, ROUND(AVG(B.EXPERIENCE_YEARS), 2) AS AVERAGE_YEARS FROM PROJECT AS A INNER JOIN EMPLOYEE AS B ON A.EMPLOYEE_ID = B.EMPLOYEE_ID GROUP BY A.PROJECT_ID
q2: SELECT C.PROJECT_ID, ROUND(AVG(C.EXPERIENCE_YEARS),2) AS AVERAGE_YEARS FROM ( SELECT A.*,B.EXPERIENCE_YEARS FROM PROJECT A LEFT JOIN EMPLOYEE B ON A.EMPLOYEE_ID=B.EMPLOYEE_ID) AS C GROUP BY 1

explanation: Q1 uses an INNER JOIN, which means it only considers projects that have at least one employee assigned to them. Q2 uses a LEFT JOIN, which means it considers all projects, including those without any employees assigned to them, and assigns NULL for the experience years of such projects.
